text:
sre-bot: PagerDuty P1 triggered for us-west-2a — high error rate from inference fleet (observability alert: 5xx spike, increased DNS latency). Root: suspected AZ-local resolver slowpath + handful of nodes losing TCP connections :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): seeing ~15% 502/504 from the edge -> inference. Traces show `rpc econnreset` from runtime to model-backend and spikes in DNS lookup times (200ms -> 2s).

jun (runtime): confirmed logs: `kvcache_populate_timeout` correlated with resolver slow replies. Dump from one runtime: 
```
Jun: 03:12:08 INF connection error: dial tcp 10.0.12.45:50051: i/o timeout
Jun: 03:12:09 ERR resolver lookup: lookup model-service.local on 169.254.169.253:53: dial udp 169.254.169.253:53: i/o timeout
```

tom (infra): checking VPC level — ENI counts look fine. I see resolver pod in us-west-2a with OOMKilled restarts earlier. Could be overloaded resolver causing LP. Also host rx-queue irregularities on a subset of instances.

lisa (prod-eng): customer impact? CS reported some customers saw degraded latencies and occasional 5xx. Need to quantify.

cs-lead: we have 2 customers (alpha-tier) reporting errors in last 10m. Notified them with interim note.

maya (oncall): mitigation proposals: 1) Route new inference traffic away from us-west-2a to us-west-2b / eu-west-1 fallback pool. 2) Apply resolver failover (switch resolver mux to cross-AZ resolver IP). 3) Temporarily reduce per-instance concurrency to limit retries. Which is fastest?

tom (infra): fastest is traffic steering via routing muxer — can flip weights in ~30s. Resolver switch needs coord with infra control plane and may take a couple minutes to fully propagate. Reducing concurrency is runtime change — can be done via config push in <5 mins.

jun (runtime): I can push concurrency cap to 2 for active nodes and enable conservative backoff for client libs. That should reduce cascade retries. Also I'll increase DNS cache TTL locally to avoid repeated lookups for short term: `local_dns_ttl: 120s`

maya (oncall): do it. tom, prepare routing change. jun, push config now and post the rollout command here.

jun (runtime): rolling config push started: `kubectl -n runtime set env deployment/runtime CONCURRENCY_CAP=2 LOCAL_DNS_TTL=120` — rolling 5% -> 100% over 3m

sre-bot: Deploy started by jun at 2026-03-15T03:15:12Z.

maya (oncall): tom, status on routing muxer?

tom (infra): I set routing muxer weight: us-west-2a -> 20%, us-west-2b -> 60%, eu-west-1 -> 20%. Command: `route-muxer set-weight --pool inference --region us-west-2a=20 --region us-west-2b=60 --region eu-west-1=20`

sre-bot: Routing weights updated (audit id rmx-6885).

maya (oncall): metrics update?

jun (runtime): after concurrency cap + DNS ttl change, 5xx rate dropped from 15% -> 4% in 2m. Latency p95 improved slightly.

cs-lead: forwarded interim customer note to impacted accounts. They want ETA for full recovery.

lisa (prod-eng): quick ask — any ongoing degraded capacity for reserved customers? We should ensure Dedicated pools are untouched.

tom (infra): Dedicated pools in us-west-2a were on different subnet/pools, check shows no errors there. This is primarily the shared hostpool/resolver path.

maya (oncall): plan: keep routing weights shifted for 30m, continue rolling checks. If steady we can move to 50/50 after 15m then bring us-west-2a up gradually. Also create incident page and assign postmortem.

pagerduty: Handing off to tom (infra) for long-running mitigation at 03:22.

maya (oncall): handing off fully to tom — I'm out for a break. Tom, you're incident lead. Please update channel on major decisions.

tom (infra): taking over. Running `dig +stats model-service.local @169.254.169.253` shows high query times on resolver in us-west-2a, replies inconsistent. I'm spinning up an additional cross-AZ resolver replica and adjusting iptables to prefer cross-AZ DNS for runtime nodes. Will monitor.

jun (runtime): runtime fleet now at CONCURRENCY_CAP=2 across region. Observed backend connection resets fall from 0.8% -> 0.2% per minute.

sre-bot: Alert: customer-error-rate trending down. Current 5xx = 2.1% (was 15%).

tom (infra): new resolver pod in us-west-2b created and registered. Also I enabled resolver priority to prefer 169.254.170.200 (cross-AZ) for runtime nodess via DHCP option. Changes applied in 90s.

lisa (prod-eng): good. Can we schedule a brief customer-update note in 20 minutes summarizing impact + mitigations? cs-lead to draft.

cs-lead: draft ready: "We observed elevated error rates from some inference requests in us-west-2a between 03:12-03:40 UTC. We routed traffic to healthy pools and applied mitigations; errors have largely subsided. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a technical postmortem." Send?

maya (oncall): +1 send it.

cs-lead: sent to impacted customers at 03:33 UTC.

tom (infra): monitoring looks stable for 10m. I'm going to start gradually moving weight back: us-west-2a -> 40%, us-west-2b -> 40%, eu-west-1 -> 20%. Doing in steps to detect regression.

jun (runtime): started gradual revert of concurrency cap to previous value (5) for healthy nodes as traffic returns.

sre-bot: Observability: 5xx now at 0.9%, p95 latency back to baseline.

tom (infra): marking incident as mitigated at 03:45 UTC. Leaving a note: root cause likely resourced resolver pod in us-west-2a causing high DNS latency combined with a subset of hosts showing rx-queue stalls — resulted in connection resets for streaming RPCs.

maya (oncall): thanks team. Action items: 1) Postmortem owner: tom (infra) 2) Fix: ensure resolver autoscale and healthchecks (jun+tom) 3) Improve routing fallback automation to switch weights faster (lisa + infra) 4) Run canary for concurrency config changes (jun).

tom (infra): acknowledged. I'll open incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/6885550000 (placeholder) and assign postmortem.

sre-bot: Incident P1 cleared from active paging. If new regressions appear, page oncall.

maya (oncall): back on deck. closing handoff. Good job. :tada:

cs-lead: will follow up with customer postmortem owners once internal postmortem is done.

jun (runtime): saving log excerpts and collectd traces to the incident bundle for postmortem.

lisa (prod-eng): add performance test to simulate resolver slowpath to regression suite.

sre-bot: Incident timeline summary created and attached to incident doc.

maya (oncall): closing thread.
